45.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Radiation) A. Beta particle B. Gamma ray C. Alpha particle List II (Is) 1. Electron 2. Helium Nucleus 3. High energy photon
45.explanation: A beta particle is an electron, a gamma ray a high-energy photon and an alpha particle a helium nucleus.

46.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Hydrogen series) A. Balmer series B. Paschen series C. Lyman series List II (Region) 1. Infrared 2. Visible 3. Ultraviolet
46.explanation: The Balmer series is visible, Paschen infrared and Lyman ultraviolet.

47.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Scientist) A. Niels Bohr B. Albert Einstein C. Ernest Rutherford List II (Known for) 1. Nucleus 2. Quantized orbits 3. Photoelectric effect
47.explanation: Bohr proposed quantised orbits, Einstein explained the photoelectric effect and Rutherford discovered the nucleus.

48.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Decay) A. Gamma decay B. Alpha decay C. Beta decay List II (Emits) 1. Electron 2. Photon 3. He nucleus
48.explanation: Gamma decay emits a photon, alpha decay a helium nucleus and beta decay an electron.

49.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantity) A. Activity B. Wavelength C. Energy List II (Unit) 1. eV 2. Becquerel 3. Angstrom
49.explanation: Radioactivity is measured in becquerels, wavelength often in ångströms and particle energy in electron volts.

84.question: Match the material with its class: List I (Material) A. Glass B. Copper C. Constantan D. Silicon List II (Class) 1. Conductor 2. Insulator 3. Semiconductor 4. Alloy
84.explanation: Glass is an insulator, copper a conductor, constantan an alloy and silicon a semiconductor.

153.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantity) A. Capacitance B. Resistance C. Inductance D. Magnetic flux List II (SI unit) 1. Ohm 2. Henry 3. Farad 4. Weber
153.explanation: Capacitance is in farads, resistance ohms, inductance henries and magnetic flux webers.

154.question: Match List I with List II: List I (AC circuit with only) A. Capacitor B. Resistor C. LCR combination D. Inductor List II (Phase) 1. In phase 2. Depends on XL/XC 3. Current leads 4. Voltage leads
154.explanation: In a capacitor the current leads, in a resistor it is in phase, in an inductor the voltage leads and in an LCR circuit it depends on XL and XC.

155.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Law) A. Lenz's law B. Ampère's circuital law C. Faraday's law D. Ohm's law List II (Gives) 1. V = IR 2. Direction of EMF 3. Magnitude of EMF 4. B field around wire
155.explanation: Lenz's law gives the direction of induced EMF, Faraday's law its magnitude, Ampère's law the field around a current and Ohm's law V = IR.

156.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Device) A. Fuse B. Transformer C. Galvanometer D. Capacitor List II (Function) 1. Current detection 2. Voltage change 3. Current limit 4. Energy storage
156.explanation: A fuse limits current, a transformer changes voltage, a galvanometer detects current and a capacitor stores energy.

157.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantity) A. Capacitive reactance B. Impedance of LCR circuit C. Inductive reactance D. Resonant frequency List II (Formula) 1. 1/(2πfC) 2. sqrt(R² + (XL-XC)²) 3. 2πfL 4. 1/(2π√LC)
157.explanation: XC = 1/(2πfC), Z = √(R² + (XL - XC)²), XL = 2πfL and f₀ = 1/(2π√LC).

205.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Wave) A. Microwaves B. X-rays C. Radio waves D. Infrared List II (Application) 1. Broadcasting 2. Night Vision 3. Radar 4. Medical Imaging
205.explanation: Microwaves are used in radar, X-rays in medical imaging, radio waves in broadcasting and infrared in night vision.

206.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Wave) A. Visible light B. Gamma rays C. Radio waves D. X-rays List II (Source) 1. Nuclear decay 2. Atomic excitation 3. Electron transition 4. Oscillating circuits
206.explanation: Visible light comes from excited atoms, gamma rays from nuclear decay, radio waves from oscillating circuits and X-rays from inner-electron transitions.

207.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Wave) A. Heat (thermal) radiation B. Lowest frequency C. Used for sterilisation D. Highest frequency List II (Property) 1. Radio waves 2. Ultraviolet 3. Infrared 4. Gamma rays
207.explanation: Infrared is felt as heat, radio waves have the lowest frequency, ultraviolet sterilises and gamma rays have the highest frequency.

209.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Wave) A. Infrared B. X-rays C. Ultraviolet D. Gamma rays List II (Effect / use) 1. Cancer therapy 2. Bone imaging 3. Sunburn 4. Heating
209.explanation: Infrared heats, X-rays image bones, ultraviolet causes sunburn and gamma rays are used in cancer therapy.

242.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Modulation) A. FM B. AM C. PCM D. PM List II (What changes) 1. Frequency varies 2. Amplitude varies 3. Digital coding 4. Phase varies
242.explanation: In FM the frequency varies, in AM the amplitude, in PM the phase, and PCM codes the signal digitally.

243.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Component) A. Demodulator B. Modulator C. Filter D. Amplifier List II (Function) 1. Extracts original signal 2. Removes unwanted frequencies 3. Combines signal and carrier 4. Increases signal strength
243.explanation: A demodulator recovers the original signal, a modulator combines signal and carrier, a filter removes unwanted frequencies and an amplifier boosts the signal.

244.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Frequency range) A. 300 kHz - 3 MHz B. 3 - 30 kHz C. 30 - 300 MHz D. 3 - 30 MHz List II (Band) 1. HF 2. VHF 3. VLF 4. MF
244.explanation: VLF is 3-30 kHz, MF 300 kHz-3 MHz, HF 3-30 MHz and VHF 30-300 MHz.

245.question: Match List I with List II: List I (PCM step) A. Quantisation B. Sampling C. Reconstruction D. Encoding List II (Description) 1. Discrete amplitude 2. Binary sequence 3. Discrete time 4. Analog recovery
245.explanation: Sampling makes time discrete, quantisation makes amplitude discrete, encoding turns it into binary and reconstruction recovers the analogue signal.

246.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Receiver / transmitter part) A. Mixer B. Oscillator C. Tuner D. Antenna List II (Use) 1. Signal radiation 2. Frequency conversion 3. Station selection 4. Generates carrier
246.explanation: A mixer converts frequency, an oscillator generates the carrier, the tuner selects a station and the antenna radiates or picks up the signal.

266.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Term) A. Electric field B. Electric potential C. Electric flux D. Coulomb's law List II (Definition) 1. Region around a charge where force acts 2. Number of electric field lines passing through a surface 3. Force between two point charges 4. Work done per unit charge to move charge
266.explanation: The electric field is the region where a charge feels force, potential is work per unit charge, flux the number of field lines through a surface and Coulomb's law gives the force between point charges.

316.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Formula) A. B = μ₀I / 2πr B. B = μ₀nI C. τ = NIAB sin θ D. F = qvB sin θ List II (For) 1. Field inside a solenoid 2. Field of a long straight wire 3. Magnetic (Lorentz) force on a charge 4. Torque on a current loop
316.explanation: B = μ₀I/2πr for a straight wire, B = μ₀nI inside a solenoid, τ = NIAB sin θ on a coil and F = qvB sin θ on a moving charge.

317.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Unit) A. Tesla B. Weber C. A m² D. Henry List II (Quantity) 1. Magnetic Flux 2. Magnetic Moment 3. Inductance 4. Magnetic Field
317.explanation: Magnetic field is in tesla, flux in weber, magnetic moment in A m² and inductance in henry.

318.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Device) A. Cyclotron B. Galvanometer C. Ammeter D. Voltmeter List II (Function) 1. Current detection 2. Voltage measurement 3. Particle acceleration 4. Current measurement
318.explanation: A cyclotron accelerates particles, a galvanometer detects current, an ammeter measures current and a voltmeter voltage.

319.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Property / use) A. Used for permanent magnets B. Used for electromagnet cores C. Diamagnetic D. Paramagnetic List II (Material) 1. Soft Iron 2. Oxygen 3. Bismuth 4. Steel
319.explanation: Steel keeps its magnetism (permanent magnets), soft iron is easily magnetised (electromagnets), bismuth is diamagnetic and oxygen paramagnetic.

339.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Term) A. Principal axis B. Focal length C. Principal focus D. Aperture List II (Description) 1. Distance from lens to focus 2. Line passing through the center of the lens 3. Diameter of the lens opening 4. Point where rays converge or appear to diverge
339.explanation: The principal axis passes through the centre of the lens, focal length is the lens-to-focus distance, the focus is where rays meet or seem to diverge from and the aperture is the opening's diameter.

344.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Phenomenon) A. Rainbow B. Dispersion C. Total internal reflection D. Mirage E. Refraction List II (Description) 1. Bending of light as it passes from one medium to another 2. Separation of light into colors 3. Apparent image of water 4. Complete reflection within a medium 5. Color bands in the sky
344.explanation: A rainbow is coloured bands in the sky, dispersion splits light into colours, total internal reflection keeps light inside a medium, a mirage looks like water and refraction is bending between media.

370.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Formula) A. tan i_p = μ B. β = λD/d C. I = I₀ cos²θ D. a sin θ = λ List II (Concept) 1. Brewster's Law 2. Malus Law 3. Fringe width 4. First minima in diffraction
370.explanation: tan i_p = μ is Brewster's law, β = λD/d the fringe width, I = I₀cos²θ Malus' law and a sin θ = λ the first diffraction minimum.

371.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Wave) A. Spherical wavefront B. Transverse wave C. Plane wavefront D. Cylindrical wavefront List II (Property) 1. Point source 2. Parallel wavefronts 3. Polarizable 4. Line source
371.explanation: A point source gives spherical wavefronts, only transverse waves can be polarised, distant sources give plane wavefronts and a line source gives cylindrical ones.

388.question: Match List I with List II: List I (Process) A. Gamma decay B. Alpha decay C. Beta decay List II (Description) 1. Emission of high energy photons 2. Emission of electron or positron 3. Emission of Helium nucleus
388.explanation: Gamma decay emits high-energy photons, alpha decay a helium nucleus and beta decay an electron or positron.
